newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY MINISTER DEFERS RESIGNATION FOR TWO WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY MINISTER DEFERS RESIGNATION FOR TWO WEEKS.

text.p: Hungary's welfare minister Gyorgy Szabo, who offered to stand down on Wednesday, said he had agreed to put off his resignation for two weeks at the request of Prime Minister Gyula Horn.
"Mr Horn and I have agreed that we should give each other two weeks to think about it," Szabo told reporters after the Cabinet's regular Thursday meeting.

Szabo is reported to have offered his resignation because of the stressful nature of his job. His department is coming under strong pressure to cut its spending as the social security deficit has widened this year to three times the 1996 target of 17.8 billion forints.

Szabo announced on Thursday that the cabinet had agreed to increase support for debt-ridden hospitals. The move follows a warning on Tuesday by the Hungarian Hospitals Federation that unless their debts are settled immediately, 49 hospitals across Hungary would run out of blood plasma and medicines.

"The government has authorised the finance minister to increase to four billion forints from two billion the funds which have been targeted for the consolidation of indebted hospitals in the draft supplmentary budget," Szabo said.
Szabo said the increase was not related to his offer of resignation.

Szabo would be the ninth minister to resign from Horn's coalition government of Socialists and Free Democrats since it was formed in May 1994. All but one have been appointees of Horn's Socialist Party.

Recent weeks have also seen the removal by Horn of the entire board of the State Privatisation Agency APV over irregular payments to a consultant and the resignation of two vice-presidents of the National Bank over an unfavourable options deal which cost the bank billions of forints.
